title: RWB-S8-E1062-APP: the deviation estate the shadow screening run reads has no read operation, no published agent-policy read, no owner role for R-DEV-05 and R-DEV-06, no value for the answer limit and no test level
source: Template and Rules v1 R5.4, R5.5, R7.2, R7.3 and R9; context pack S8 rwb-deviation; split plan story line RWB-S8-E1062-APP; legacy RWB-E1-062; FSD S8 Deviation handling v3 A2.4 and A2.7; TSD S8 Deviation handling v2 T3.1, T3.2, T4, T5.3, T6.1 and T-A.1; Architecture v5 slides 3, 4, 8 and 13
section: Metadata (Depends on (build), Contract dependencies); Sections 1, 3, 4, 5, 7, 8, 9, 11, 12.1 to 12.9, 13 and 16
description: (1) The Ownership Map gives rwb-deviation two write operations, POST /cases/{caseId}/deviations and PATCH /deviations/{deviationId}, and no read, while the shadow run must know the open codes of a case so a code already open is not proposed again (legacy DF-CAS-038) and rwb-agent's contract of this legacy key names a deviation read as its source; the read is therefore declared on the service base with a gap. (2) No source publishes the operation name or the field names of the agent-policy read the gate needs, nor a message id for a refusal no person sees. (3) The pattern set carries DP-04, DP-06, DP-07, DP-09, DP-15 and DP-19, whose DP table rows add six platform H dependencies, while the plan's H row for this secondary slice is empty. (4) Legacy AC4 publishes RW-FRAUD from R-DEV-04 for X4 and the team manager for a code with no row, but no source read for this slice prints the codes or owner roles of R-DEV-05 and R-DEV-06. (5) The maximum number of deviations one answer carries is not published, and no page size or cap exists in the sources. (6) The ten legacy test cases carry no level, and the agent half of each is RWB-P10-E1062-APP's. (7) The legacy criteria AC1 to AC9 are owned by RWB-P10-E1062-APP while the shadow rule BR1 has a producer-side half in this service, which this story proves with new criteria and no legacy AC. (8) rwb-deviation owns no job in the ownership rows, so no Schedule exists and the estate is read on request.
evidence: Context pack S8 ownership rows (Tables 1 deviation, REST 2, Events EV-06 and EV-07, Jobs 0, Workflows 1 DeviationWorkflow); TSD S8 T-A.1 two endpoints and no read; TSD S8 T5.3 two published events; TSD S8 T3.2 two lists; TSD S8 T4 22 rules over 9 states with R-DEV-04, R-DEV-05, R-DEV-06 on DEV_FLAGGED and OWNER_ASSIGNED; FSD S8 A2.4.3.1 printing the text of R-DEV-02 and R-DEV-03 only; legacy RWB-E1-062 sections 4, 11, 12, 16 and BR1, BR3, AC1, AC4; split plan RWB-S8-E1062-APP with acs empty and H empty; rwb-agent contract of RWB-P10-E1062-CON naming GET /api/recovery/deviation/v1/deviations as its open-deviation read
area: Contract; API; rules; data; test levels
owner_role: Solution architect, with the rwb-deviation owner, the rule-set owner of the Deviations package, the rwb-agent contract owner, the rwb-case parameter and reference-data owners, the ACE DB team lead and the QA lead
proposed: Publish the deviation estate read as a service operation with a catalogue row, or amend the Ownership Map to carry it; publish the operation name of the agent-policy read and bind the shadow refusal to one status; record the six platform contracts as template dependencies of S8 and keep the H row empty; publish the codes and owner roles of R-DEV-05 and R-DEV-06 with the package version; set the answer limit as a parameter value; publish the test level of the ten legacy cases and split each between RWB-P10-E1062-APP, RWB-S8-E1062-APP and RWB-ITG-E1062-ITG
